name: Outbid Directory
tagline: A curated web directory of listings you browse, search and filter by tag.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software under a directory is the least interesting part of a directory. An agent can produce the search, the tag filters, the detail pages and the dead-link checker in an afternoon, and the result will look fine and be completely empty. What you are actually paying for, or visiting for, is somebody else's accumulated judgment about what belongs on the list and what got quietly removed. That corpus is hand-assembled over months and it does not come out of a prompt. Build the shell if you want your own private list of things; do not expect it to replace someone else's.
coreLoopDIY: A static, searchable, tag-filtered directory of listings stored as Markdown files, with a CLI to add entries and a script to flag dead links.
requirements: A static host or just a local browser
Your own listings, which is the entire problem
whatYouLose: The listings, which is the product
Whoever is out there finding and vetting new entries every week
Removal of things that quietly died or turned bad
Any traffic, so if you wanted to be listed rather than to browse, a personal copy does nothing
Whatever ranking or editorial ordering the original applies
moatNotes: Directories are two-sided in a quiet way: listers show up because visitors do, and visitors show up because the list is already good.
whyPeopleStillPay: Directories get paid because they concentrate attention. If people pay to be listed, they are buying discovery from an audience that already trusts the list, and no amount of self-hosted Astro produces an audience. If people pay to browse, they are buying somebody else's filtering time, which is the only genuinely scarce input here. The build is trivial and the moat is entirely non-technical, which is the least satisfying kind of moat to run into.
notes: The directory software is an afternoon; the directory is not. The moat is the curated list itself plus the traffic that makes being on it worth anything.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted curated directory site I can run locally and deploy as static files.

Stack: Astro 4 with TypeScript, Tailwind, and content collections. No database, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics.

Data model: each listing is a Markdown file in src/content/listings with frontmatter: name, url, oneLiner, tags (string array), price (string or null), status (active or dead), addedOn (date). The Markdown body is my private notes on the entry.

Pages:
- / : searchable, filterable grid of all active listings. Client side search with Fuse.js over name, oneLiner and tags. Tag chips filter with multi select, and filter state lives in the URL query string so I can bookmark a view.
- /listing/[slug] : detail page rendering the notes body, the outbound link with rel="nofollow noopener", the tags, and the addedOn date.
- /tags/[tag] : statically generated index per tag.
- /submit : a plain page with a mailto link only. Do not build a form backend.

CLI: scripts/add.ts, run with tsx. It prompts for name and url, fetches the page, uses the page title and meta description as defaults for name and oneLiner, asks for tags, then writes the Markdown file with a slugified filename.

CLI: scripts/check-links.ts. Fetch every listing url, set status to dead in the frontmatter for anything that is not a 2xx after one retry, and print a summary table.

Validation: Zod schema on the content collection. Fail the build on missing fields, malformed dates, or duplicate urls.

Seed with 8 plausible example listings so the UI is not empty on first run.

Deliver a README with dev, build, add and check-links commands. Output must be a fully static site in dist/ that works on any static host. No secrets are needed, so do not create a .env file.
